nodes.title: Soundness and relative completeness of certificates
nodes.statement: A valid five-term certificate for the difference of two finite combinations proves that they have the same class in P(F). Conversely, if two combinations have the same class in P(F), then some valid certificate for their difference exists. Existence is not effective: no bound on the length of the certificate is claimed.
hypotheses: F is a field.
proofSteps: Soundness: the evaluation of a certificate lies in the five-term subgroup by construction, so the classes agree.

Completeness: equality of classes means the difference lies in the five-term subgroup, and every element of a subgroup generated by a set is a finite integer combination of its generators, which is exactly a certificate.
Record the honest limitation: the completeness statement is pure existence, with no length bound and no search procedure, and this is stated rather than hidden.
acceptance: Soundness is checked on the certificate for the independence of c from its parameter.
Completeness is used only to justify the format, never to produce a certificate.
No complexity claim is made; a claimed bound would be an unproved addition.

nodes.title: Lifting a certified Bloch element to K_3 and to bar cycles
nodes.statement: Let F be an infinite field and β an element of B(F) produced by V.6/bloch-element-constructor. Then there is a class z ∈ H_3(GL_3(F), Z) with ψ(z) = β, and a class k ∈ K_3(F) ≅ H_3(St(F), Z), represented by a bar 3-cycle of the stable Steinberg group, whose image under K_3(F) → K_3^ind(F) → B(F) is β. The class z is determined up to the image of H_3(M_2, Z) ⊕ H_3(T_3, Z), and k up to the kernel of K_3(F) → B(F), which contains K_3^M(F) and the image of µ̃(F); a five-term certificate relating two inputs changes the lift only within this ambiguity. The statement is existence: no source read constructs an explicit bar cycle from a certificate (gap).
hypotheses: F is an infinite field, as in V.4/psi-gl3 and V.4/homological-stability.
proofSteps: Existence of z: ψ: H_3(GL_3(F), Z) → B(F) is onto with kernel the image of H_3(M_2) ⊕ H_3(T_3) (V.4/psi-gl3), and H_3(GL_3(F)) ≅ H_3(GL(F)) (V.4/homological-stability).
Existence of k: K_3(F) → K_3^ind(F) → B(F) is onto (V.4/suslin-exact-sequence) and agrees with ψ composed with the homological model (V.4/suslin-functoriality).
Representation: every class of K_3(F) = H_3(St(F), Z) is the class of a bar 3-cycle (V.1/k3-h3-steinberg, V.1/bar-cycle-model).

Ambiguity: the kernel of K_3(F) → B(F) is generated by the decomposable image and µ̃(F) (V.2/decomposable-exactness, V.4/suslin-exact-sequence); inputs related by a valid five-term certificate give the same β (V.6/bloch-element-constructor), hence lifts in the same coset.
Record the gap: an explicit chain-level lift of β through the hyperhomology spectral sequence, and from H_3(GL(F)) to H_3(St(F)), is not given by the sources read.
acceptance: A certificate for the zero element yields β = 0, whose lifts are exactly the kernel of K_3(F) → B(F).
For Q, every lift of c to K_3(Q) ≅ Z/48 is a generator, of order 48, and every lift to K_3^ind(Q) ≅ Z/24 has order 24: the lift of an element of order six need not have order dividing six.
The lift is not canonical, and the comparison states this rather than choosing one.

nodes.title: When a root-of-unity symbol lies in the Bloch group
nodes.statement: Let F be a field and ζ ∈ F a root of unity of exact order m ≥ 2. Then m · ∂[ζ] = 0 in ∧̃²F^×, so m[ζ] ∈ B(F); and [ζ] ∈ B(F) if and only if ζ ∧ (1 − ζ) = 0 in ∧̃²F^×. For a primitive sixth root of unity ω one has 1 − ω = ω^{−1} and ∂[ω] = (−1) ∧ (−1), so [ω] ∈ B(F) if and only if −1 is a square in F. All statements are in Suslin's convention of V.3; in the exterior-square convention ∂[ω] is always zero.
hypotheses: F is a field.
ζ ∈ F is a root of unity of exact order m ≥ 2.
proofSteps: ∂[ζ] = ζ ∧ (1 − ζ) by V.3/bloch-boundary, and m(ζ ⊗ (1 − ζ)) = ζ^m ⊗ (1 − ζ) = 0 in F^× ⊗ F^×; so m[ζ] lies in the kernel B(F).
[ζ] ∈ B(F) if and only if its boundary vanishes, by the definition of B(F) (V.3/bloch-group).
For ω of exact order 6, ω² − ω + 1 = 0 gives 1 − ω = −ω² = ω^{−1}, so ∂[ω] = −(ω ∧ ω); writing ω = (ω²)² · (−1) and using (ab) ∧ (ab) = a ∧ a + b ∧ b and 2(a ∧ a) = 0 gives ω ∧ ω = (−1) ∧ (−1).
By V.3/antisym-exterior-comparison, a ↦ a ∧ a is injective on F^×/F^{×2}, so (−1) ∧ (−1) = 0 exactly when −1 is a square.
acceptance: Over Q(√−3), [ω] ∉ B(F) but 2[ω] ∈ B(F); over Q(ζ_12), which contains i, [ω] ∈ B(F).
Over Q(i), ∂[i] = i ∧ (1 − i) has order four, so 4[i] is the least positive multiple in B(Q(i)).
A regulator is never applied to [ζ] itself unless the criterion holds; otherwise the classes of V.6/root-of-unity-class are used.

nodes.title: The rational comparison
nodes.statement: For every field F with at least four elements, tensoring Suslin's sequence with Q gives an isomorphism K_3^ind(F) ⊗ Q ≅ B(F) ⊗ Q, natural in F. The comparison κ of V.3/cgz-convention-comparison between Suslin's and CGZ's Bloch groups has kernel and cokernel annihilated by 2, so it becomes an isomorphism after tensoring with Q and both conventions give the same rational answer. For a number field K_3(F) ⊗ Q = K_3^ind(F) ⊗ Q, of dimension r_2.
hypotheses: F is a field with at least four elements.
proofSteps: Tensor Suslin's sequence (V.4/suslin-exact-sequence) with Q; µ̃(F) is torsion, so it dies and the remaining map is an isomorphism.
Naturality in F is V.4/suslin-functoriality tensored with Q.
κ ⊗ Q is an isomorphism because the kernel and cokernel of κ are killed by 2 (V.3/cgz-convention-comparison).
For a number field, combine with V.2/rationalisation-loss and V.5/k3-number-field.
State the prohibition: an agreement of two models rationally is not evidence for an integral comparison.
acceptance: For a finite field both sides vanish rationally, so the comparison is vacuous there.
For a number field both sides have dimension r_2.
The comparison cannot see that κ is not surjective over F_11 (image of order three in CGZ's B(F_11) ≅ Z/6) or that κ(c) has order three in CGZ's B(Q) while c has order six in B(Q).

nodes.title: The integral comparison, with torsion retained
nodes.statement: For every field F with at least four elements, export Suslin's sequence 0 → µ̃(F) → K_3^ind(F) → B(F) → 0 integrally, with B(F) in Suslin's convention of V.3 and µ̃(F) the enhanced group of V.4, not Tor_1(µ(F), µ(F)). The sequence need not split (for Q it is 0 → Z/4 → Z/24 → Z/6 → 0), so K_3^ind(F) and B(F) are not interchangeable integrally. The comparison κ of V.3 with CGZ's Bloch group has kernel and cokernel killed by 2 but is in general neither injective nor surjective; the sequence with CGZ's group in place of B(F) is therefore not asserted integrally, and consumers of CGZ's group use κ together with the odd-coefficient comparison of V.6/comparison-finite-coefficients.
hypotheses: F is a field with at least four elements.
proofSteps: Export the sequence of V.4/suslin-exact-sequence with its left-hand term named and its enhancement recorded (V.4/enhanced-mu, V.4/tor-form-comparison).
Export κ of V.3/cgz-convention-comparison with its 2-torsion kernel and cokernel.
Record the worked example for Q from V.5/k3-Q-splitting, where the orders 4, 24 and 6 make the non-split extension visible.
Record that κ is not a quotient map: over F_11 its image in CGZ's B(F_11) ≅ Z/6 has order three, and over Q it sends c, of order six, to [0], of order three.
State the two prohibitions the roadmap requires: the enhanced term is not the ordinary Tor group, and the Bloch group is not a substitute for K_3^ind integrally.
acceptance: For Q the extension of Z/6 by Z/4 is non-split, since the middle group is cyclic of order 24.
For a field of characteristic two the enhanced term equals µ(F), which has odd order, so the enhancement is invisible there; the export says so.

Over F_11: B(F_11) ≅ Z/6, CGZ's B(F_11) ≅ Z/6, and κ has image of order three (Smith normal form of both presentations; the same holds for q = 7, 19, 27, and κ is an isomorphism for q = 4, 5, 8, 9, 13, 17, 25).
Over Q, κ(c) = [0] has order three (CGZ Definition 1.1 and (34) with n = 3), so κ is not injective on B(Q) ≅ Z/6.

nodes.title: The comparisons modulo n
nodes.statement: Let F be a field with at least four elements and n ≥ 1. Reducing Suslin's sequence modulo n gives the exact sequence 0 → µ̃(F)[n] → K_3^ind(F)[n] → B(F)[n] → µ̃(F)/n → K_3^ind(F)/n → B(F)/n → 0. Hence K_3^ind(F)/n → B(F)/n is onto with kernel the image of µ̃(F)/n. If n is odd and µ(F) ⊗ Z/n = 0, it is an isomorphism. For odd n, κ of V.3 induces B(F)/n ≅ B_CGZ(F)/n. For a number field F and odd n, K_3(F)/n ≅ K_3^ind(F)/n, since K_3^M(F) ≅ (Z/2)^{r_1}; so if F contains no primitive p-th root of unity for any prime p dividing n, then K_3(F)/n ≅ B(F)/n ≅ B_CGZ(F)/n, which is the left-hand column of CGZ Lemma 4.4. Without that hypothesis the identification fails, and for even n no identification is asserted.
hypotheses: F is a field with at least four elements; n is a positive integer.
For the isomorphisms: n odd and µ(F) ⊗ Z/n = 0; for a number field, F contains no primitive p-th root of unity for p | n.
proofSteps: Apply Tor(−, Z/n) and − ⊗ Z/n to V.4/suslin-exact-sequence to obtain the six-term sequence.
For odd n, µ̃(F)/n = µ(F)/n, because the enhancement is by Z/2 (V.4/enhanced-mu); so µ(F) ⊗ Z/n = 0 gives the isomorphism.
For odd n, κ ⊗ Z/n is an isomorphism because the kernel and cokernel of κ are killed by 2 (V.3/cgz-convention-comparison); this is the reduction CGZ make at the start of the proof of Theorem 2.11.

For a number field, K_3^M(F) is 2-torsion (V.2/milnor-k3-number-field), so K_3(F)/n → K_3^ind(F)/n is an isomorphism for odd n (V.2/decomposable-exactness); µ(F) is finite cyclic, and µ(F) ⊗ Z/n = 0 exactly when F contains no primitive p-th root of unity for p | n.
Counterexample to dropping the hypothesis, from V.5/k3-number-field: for F = Q(√−3) and n = 3, K_3(F) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/24 and µ̃(F) ≅ Z/12, so B(F) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/2 and B(F)/3 ≅ Z/3, while K_3(F)/3 ≅ (Z/3)².
Record the consumers: HabiroNumberFields HB.1 and HB.2 and PadicHodgeRegulators D.2 use these reductions, not the rational comparison.
acceptance: For odd n the two conventions give the same group modulo n.
For Q(√−3) and n = 3 the map K_3(F)/3 → B(F)/3 is not injective.
For n = 2 and F = Q(i): K_3^ind(F) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/24, µ̃(F) ≅ Z/8 and B(F) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/3, so K_3^ind(F)/2 ≅ (Z/2)² while B(F)/2 ≅ Z/2.
For a finite field F_q and odd n prime to q − 1 the comparison is V.5/bloch-finite-field-mod-n.

nodes.title: Agreement of the real regulator with the Borel regulator
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field. The weight-two regulator of Polylogarithms P.2 (the Bloch-Wigner descent assembled over the complex places, Polylogarithms:P.2/weight-two-regulator), composed with the Suslin map K_3(F) → K_3^ind(F) → B(F), agrees with the Borel regulator on K_3(F) up to the sign and the nonzero rational scalar fixed in Polylogarithms:P.2/borel-comparison. Both maps kill K_3(F)_tors, so the statement is equivalent to its rationalisation through V.6/comparison-rational and says nothing about which integral Bloch-group convention is used. The analytic comparison is P.2's; this node only transports it along V.6's rational comparison.
hypotheses: F is a number field.
proofSteps: Import Polylogarithms:P.2/borel-comparison, which compares the weight-two regulator with the Borel regulator on K_3^ind(F) under Suslin's sequence.
Compose with the quotient K_3(F) → K_3^ind(F) (V.2/k3-indecomposable); the decomposable part is torsion and is killed.
Rewrite the statement through V.6/comparison-rational: both sides factor through K_3(F) ⊗ Q ≅ B(F) ⊗ Q.
Record that no integral statement follows, as the stage text of Polylogarithms P.2 also says.
acceptance: The real regulator kills torsion, so it agrees with the Borel regulator only after the rational comparison.
For a totally real field both sides vanish.
No claim is made that the regulator is nonzero on a specific element; that is P.2's certified-numerics node.

nodes.title: A vanishing-boundary certificate
nodes.statement: Let F be a field and ξ = Σ n_x [x] a finitely supported integer combination of elements x ∈ F − {0, 1}. A vanishing-boundary certificate for ξ consists of a root of unity ζ_0 ∈ F^× with its exact order m_0 ≥ 1, elements g_1, …, g_s ∈ F^×, and for each x in the support exponent vectors e(x), f(x) ∈ Z/m_0 × Z^s with x = ζ_0^{e_0} ∏ g_j^{e_j} and 1 − x = ζ_0^{f_0} ∏ g_j^{f_j} (equalities in F). Its boundary is Σ n_x e(x) ∧ f(x) in ∧̃²(Z/m_0 × Z^s) ≅ Z/gcd(m_0, 2) ⊕ (Z/m_0)^s ⊕ (Z/2)^s ⊕ Z^{s(s−1)/2}, with components Σ n_x e_0 f_0 mod gcd(m_0, 2), Σ n_x (e_0 f_j − e_j f_0) mod m_0, Σ n_x e_j f_j mod 2 and Σ n_x (e_j f_k − e_k f_j) for j < k. The certificate is valid when all components vanish. A valid certificate proves ∂ξ = 0 in ∧̃²F^×; if ζ_0 and the g_j generate a direct summand of F^× on which they are a basis, the converse holds.
hypotheses: F is a field; ξ is supported on F − {0, 1}.
ζ_0 has exact order m_0; the displayed factorisations hold in F.
proofSteps: Define the data and the explicit boundary formula; the formula is well defined because e_0 and f_0 are only determined modulo m_0 and each component is taken modulo a divisor of m_0 or does not involve them.
Soundness: the homomorphism Z/m_0 × Z^s → F^× sending the basis to ζ_0, g_1, …, g_s induces ∧̃²(Z/m_0 × Z^s) → ∧̃²F^× and sends the boundary to ∂ξ of V.3/bloch-boundary.

The computation of ∧̃² of Z/m_0 × Z^s is the definition of the antisymmetric quotient (V.3/antisymmetric-tensor-quotient) applied to a basis: a ∧ b + b ∧ a = 0 on basis elements generates all relations.
Completeness on a direct summand: ∧̃² of a direct summand is a direct summand of ∧̃²F^×, so the map is injective there.
Validity is decidable: it is finitely many congruences and integer equations.
acceptance: The certificate for c over Q is valid.
The data for [2] over Q is not valid, and because ⟨−1, 2⟩ is a direct summand of Q^× this proves [2] ∉ B(Q).
The certificate detects the convention: over Q(√−3) the data for [ω] fails the (0, 0) component, which has no counterpart in the exterior square.

nodes.title: Valid classes attached to a root of unity
nodes.statement: Let ζ ∈ F be a root of unity of exact order m ≥ 2. (i) For n ≥ 1 prime to m, define ⟦ζ⟧_n ∈ B(F)/nB(F) as u · (m[ζ]) with u m ≡ 1 mod n; it does not depend on u and maps to the class of [ζ] in P(F)/nP(F). (ii) Define ⟦ζ⟧[1/m] ∈ B(F) ⊗ Z[1/m] as m^{−1} ⊗ m[ζ]; it maps to [ζ] ⊗ 1 in P(F) ⊗ Z[1/m]. (iii) For a prime p not dividing m, define the class in B(F) ⊗ Z_p in the same way. When [ζ] ∈ B(F) (V.6/root-of-unity-symbol) each class is the image of [ζ]; otherwise none is the image of an element [ζ] of B(F). These are the substitutes the consumers use in place of [ζ].
hypotheses: F is a field; ζ ∈ F has exact order m ≥ 2.
n is prime to m, respectively p does not divide m.
proofSteps: m[ζ] ∈ B(F) by V.6/root-of-unity-symbol; produce it with V.6/bloch-element-constructor.
Independence of u: changing u by a multiple of n changes the class by a multiple of n · m[ζ] ∈ nB(F).
In P(F)/nP(F) the class of u m [ζ] is the class of [ζ], because u m ≡ 1 mod n.
Z[1/m] and Z_p (p ∤ m) are flat, so B(F) ⊗ Z[1/m] is the kernel of the boundary on P(F) ⊗ Z[1/m], which contains [ζ] ⊗ 1 because ∂[ζ] is m-torsion; the same for Z_p.
Compatibility: the image of ⟦ζ⟧[1/m] in B(F) ⊗ Z/n is ⟦ζ⟧_n.
acceptance: Over Q, ⟦−1⟧_3 = 0 in B(Q)/3B(Q).
Over Q(√−3), ⟦ω⟧_5 is defined although [ω] ∉ B(F).
PadicHodgeRegulators D.3's roots-of-unity classes, of order prime to p in an unramified extension of Q_p, are the classes (iii).

nodes.title: Agreement of the p-adic regulator under the comparison modulo p^m
nodes.statement: Let p > 3, let L be a finite unramified extension of Q_p (the setting of PadicHodgeRegulators D.2 and D.3) and n = p^m. The comparison of PadicHodgeRegulators D.2 between the syntomic or étale regulator in degree three and weight two and the p-adic dilogarithm on the Bloch-group model is transported to K_3^ind(L)/n through V.6/comparison-finite-coefficients: since p is odd and ζ_p ∉ L (Q_p(ζ_p) is totally ramified of degree p − 1 > 1), K_3^ind(L)/n ≅ B(L)/n in either convention of V.3. Roots-of-unity inputs are the classes of V.6/root-of-unity-class. The passage from K_3(L)/n to K_3^ind(L)/n needs K_3^M(L)/n = 0 or that the regulator kills decomposables; neither is supplied by a stage read (gap).
hypotheses: p > 3; L is a finite unramified extension of Q_p; n = p^m.
proofSteps: Import the degree-three, weight-two comparison of PadicHodgeRegulators D.2, whose stage text reads 'In degree three and weight two compare the regulator with the explicit p-adic dilogarithm on V's Bloch-group model. Give the actual scalar/Frobenius normalisation.'
µ(L) ⊗ Z/p = 0 because ζ_p ∉ L, so V.6/comparison-finite-coefficients gives K_3^ind(L)/n ≅ B(L)/n, and κ ⊗ Z/n identifies the two conventions.

The e-invariant detection (K-book Lemma VI.5.19) needs étale Chern classes, which only MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8 plans, downstream of V.4 (gap and restructure proposal).
Steps the K-book leaves to Suslin [187] and [183]: the d³ computation, the vanishing of ψ′, ker ψ in rank two, the 2-primary part of H₃(Σ₆) and the Künneth summands (gaps).
Stable-homotopy inputs to the monomial-group computation: Barratt–Priddy–Quillen, the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence over π^s_*, π^s_3/(η³) and H₃(Σ_∞) (gap).
The Künneth formula for group homology, used for T₂, M₂ × Σ_{n−2}, GL(F) and SM, is in neither library and is planned by no stage (gap).

gaps.title: Suslin's original paper was not obtained
gaps.detail: Suslin, 'K₃ of a field, and the Bloch group', Trudy Mat. Inst. Steklov 183 (1990), 180–199, English translation Proc. Steklov Inst. Math. (1991), 217–239 (K-book reference [187], PDF p. 573), was not read. The K-book reproduces the proof of Theorem VI.5.2 from it but leaves four steps to it: the d³ computation ('A routine but tedious calculation shows that the differential d3 : P(F) → H2(T2)σ is the canonical map … see [187, 2.4]', PDF p. 499); the kernel of ψ on H₃(GL₂) ('Suslin showed in [187, p. 223] that K is the image', p. 499); the vanishing of ψ′ on (DG)₄ ('by a straightforward calculation done in [187, 3.3]', p. 501); and the Rogers-function argument for the order of c ([187, pp. 219–220], p. 496; see the gap on the order of c). The two steps previously listed here, on H₃(Σ₆) and on the Künneth summands of the relative monomial term, are cited by the K-book to Suslin [183], not to [187], and are now in the homological-stability gap. A continuation that obtains [187] should check these four.

gaps.title: Hilton–Milnor and Whitehead-product inputs to Suslin's degree-three Hurewicz sequence
gaps.detail: V.1/eta-hurewicz-sequence (K-book Lemma IV.1.19 and Remark IV.1.19.1) needs: the Hilton–Milnor description of π_3 of a wedge of 2-spheres (generated by the Hopf classes and the Whitehead products [ι_i, ι_j], i < j), the vanishing of Whitehead products in an H-space (Whitehead, Elements of Homotopy Theory, X(7.8)), and Ex. IV.1.25 (exactness of π_3(Y) → π_3(X) → H_3(X) → 0 when π_2(Y) → π_2(X) is onto). No stage of StableHomotopyKTheory or the Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology roadmap states them.

gaps.title: The Hopf element and the product with [−1] (Ex. IV.1.12(a),(e))
gaps.detail: V.1/k2-to-k3-h3-e identifies composition with η on π_2(BE(R)⁺) with the product with [−1] ∈ K_1(Z). This needs the map BΣ∞⁺ → BGL(Z)⁺ and the ring map from the stable stems to K_*(Z) with η ↦ [−1] (Ex. IV.1.12(a)), and the agreement of composition products with products by stable classes (Ex. IV.1.12(e)). No stage plans them.

gaps.title: Bass–Tate: Milnor K-theory of a number field in degrees at least three
gaps.detail: V.2/milnor-k3-number-field needs K_n^M(F) ≅ (Z/2)^{r_1} for n ≥ 3 (K-book III.7.2(d), citing Bass–Tate, 'The Milnor ring of a global field', 1973, which was not read). K2SymbolsBrauer T.2 plans only the definition of Milnor K-theory and Matsumoto's theorem; the V.2 stage text itself owns the specialisation ('Milnor K₃ of a number field is controlled by its real places and is torsion'), so it must be decomposed here from the original source.

gaps.title: Motivic Chern classes c_{i,i} and Lemma V.11.13
gaps.detail: V.2/milnor-k3-kernel-exponent-two needs the Chern classes c_{i,i} : K_i(F) → H^{i,i}(F) ≅ K_i^M(F) with their product rule (K-book V.11.3, V.11.11) and Lemma V.11.13. MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8 plans étale Chern classes only; no stage states the motivic ones.

gaps.title: Izhboldin's theorem
gaps.detail: The characteristic-two case of V.2/milnor-k3-injective needs that K_n^M(F) has no p-torsion when char F = p (K-book III.7.8, PDF p. 259). No stage plans it.

gaps.title: The weight-two, degree-zero norm residue identification
gaps.detail: V.2/milnor-k3-injective needs H^0(k, Z/2(2)) ≅ H^0_et(k, μ_2^{⊗2}) = Z/2 for char k ≠ 2 (the case n = 0 ≤ i = 2 of the K-book's Theorem VI.4.1). MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5 states only the Bloch–Kato form K_j^M(F)/ℓ^r ≅ H^j(F, μ^{⊗j}), from which the motivic-to-étale comparison is a further theorem.

gaps.title: Divisibility for algebraically closed fields
gaps.detail: V.2/milnor-k3-injective needs that K_4 of an algebraically closed field is divisible (K-book VI.1.6 in characteristic 0 and Corollary VI.1.3.1(i) in characteristic p > 0) and that K_n^M of an algebraically closed field is uniquely divisible (III.7.2(b)). No stage states either.

gaps.title: Hurewicz and covering-space inputs owned by upstream Tau Ceti roadmaps
gaps.detail: The absolute Hurewicz theorem ('an (n-1)-connected pointed space has reduced integral homology zero below n and pi_n(X) ~= H_n(X;Z) for n>=2') and its naturality are planned by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology#stage-8-relative-homotopy-hurewicz-and-whitehead, and the H-space structure on the universal cover of a connected H-space follows from the lifting criterion of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers#stage-2-lifting-criterion-and-galois-correspondence. These atlas stage ids cannot be listed as prerequisites, because scripts/check_blueprint.py parses every tauceti:-prefixed id as a baseline declaration; they are cited here and through the request to the AlgebraicTopology stage.

gaps.title: Bloch's and Goncharov's Bloch-group conventions are not planned
gaps.detail: The V.3 stage text reads: 'Separately construct the conventions used by Bloch, Goncharov and Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier. Prove the comparison maps, their exact small torsion corrections and their rational identifications.' Only the CGZ convention is planned (cgz-bloch-group, cgz-convention-comparison). CGZ (p. 2) call their Definition 1.1 'the classical Bloch group, as introduced in [2]', i.e. Bloch's, but Bloch's lectures were not read, so this identification is unverified. Goncharov's B_2(F) (ℤ[P^1(F)] modulo the five-term relations of cross-ratios of five points) was not read at all. Any convention that sets [0] = 0 sends c to 0, a discrepancy of 3-torsion as well as 2-torsion from Suslin's; this is the '6-torsion' CGZ mention. Needed: the two sources (Bloch, Higher regulators, algebraic K-theory, and zeta functions of elliptic curves; Goncharov, Geometry of configurations, polylogarithms, and motivic cohomology, Adv. Math. 114 (1995)), a definition node for each convention, and a comparison node for each, with its exact torsion correction.

gaps.title: Hyperhomology spectral sequence and group-homology tools for V.4
gaps.detail: V.4 uses the first-quadrant spectral sequence of the double complex P ⊗_G C_*(X) with its convergence and edge maps, the Künneth formula for H_*(A × B, ℤ), H_2(A, ℤ) ≅ ∧²A for abelian A, the Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for discrete groups, the triviality of inner automorphisms on group homology, and transfer (corestriction) with the Sylow argument. No atlas stage owns them: the Hochschild–Serre owners are continuous and profinite (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2), and StableHomotopyKTheory H.6 builds spectral sequences of filtered spectra, not of double complexes of group modules. Mathlib 082e2d3 has HomologicalComplex₂.total, Shapiro's lemma groupHomology.indIso and the periodic resolution Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.resolution, but only the abstract spectral-object framework (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/SpectralObject/*.lean) and no Künneth formula for group homology. (Merged by the review with a parallel finding: V.4 computes the homology of products of groups by the Künneth formula: H_n(T₂) from H_*(Fˣ) (K-book 5.8.2, PDF p. 499, 'By the Künneth formula [223, 6.1.13]'); the relative monomial term of H₃(M₂ × Σ_{n−2}) (proof of Proposition 5.15, p. 504); and the splittings H_nGL(F) ≅ ⊕ H_iSL(F) ⊗ H_jFˣ and H₃SM ≅ H₃P ⊕ (H₂P ⊗ H₁Σ₂) ⊕ H₃Σ₂ (proof of Theorem 5.16, pp. 504–505). Neither pinned library has a Künneth theorem for group homology (no declaration mentions it), and no atlas stage plans one. The Tau Ceti roadmap AlgebraicTopology plans the Künneth spectral sequence for spaces (stage 5), which gives it through BG × BH ≃ B(G × H) and StableHomotopyKTheory H.1's comparison of bar homology with singular homology; that roadmap cannot be listed as a prerequisite (tauceti: ids are read as baseline declarations). The integral statement must keep the Tor summand ⊕_{i+j=n−1} Tor₁^ℤ(H_i(G), H_j(H)); see the source issue on 5.8.2.)

gaps.title: Suslin's comparison of the torus and the Borel subgroup
gaps.detail: The isomorphism H_*(T_2, ℤ) ≅ H_*(B_2, ℤ) for infinite F is cited by the K-book from Suslin, Homology of GL_n, characteristic classes and Milnor K-theory [184, §3], without proof, and the paper was not obtained. It is false for F_4 in degree two, so the proof must use that F is infinite.

gaps.title: Further steps of Suslin's proof not reproduced in the K-book
gaps.detail: In addition to the three steps of the existing gap on Suslin's paper: the identification of d^3 with the Bloch boundary ([187, 2.4], 'a routine but tedious calculation'); the vanishing of ψ′ on d((D_G)_4) ([187, 3.3]; checked here by computer in P(F_p) for p = 7, …, 19 with ψ′(P) = −2c); the triviality of H_*(A_3) → H_*(GL_3(F)) in characteristic three ([181]); and a derivation of the Dupont–Sah identities (K-book Exercise VI.5.5, whose second identity is misprinted).

gaps.title: Homological stability for infinite fields is owned by V.4 but not decomposed
gaps.detail: The V.4 stage asks to prove the homology-stability lemmas 'here when they are not supplied by H'. No stage supplies them: StableHomotopyKTheory H.3 is the plus construction, GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2:plus the ring and plus model, and the stage-level GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2 that the packet cited is a descendant of V.4 (K.2 requires K.2:low-degree-comparisons, which requires V.4). The K-book states Suslin's theorem (Proposition IV.1.15) and the generation statement [183, 3.4] without proof; Suslin's paper [183] was not obtained. (Merged by the review with a parallel finding: V.4's stage text assigns this lemma to V.4: 'Record which homology-stability and configuration-acyclicity lemmas it uses, and prove them here when they are not supplied by H.' No stage of StableHomotopyKTheory states it (H.1 to H.6 were read; H.3 plans only the plus construction). GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2 does not state it either, and cannot be a prerequisite of V.4 because its part K.2:low-degree-comparisons requires K3BlochGroups V.4. So the current prerequisites of V.4/homological-stability supply nothing, and the lemma is owned here. The K-book states it without proof: 'Proposition 1.15. (Suslin) If F is an infinite field, then Hn(GLr(F)) → Hn(GL(F)) is an isomorphism for all r ≥ n. In addition, there is a canonical isomorphism Hn(GLn(F))/im Hn(GLn−1(F)) ≅ K^M_n(F)' (IV.1.15, PDF p. 278, citing [183]). The source, Suslin, 'Homology of GL_n, characteristic classes and Milnor K-theory', Lecture Notes in Math. 1046 (1984), 357–375 (K-book [183]), was not read. V.4 takes three further steps from the same paper as the K-book states them: 'By [183, 3.4], H3(T3, Z) and H3(GL2, Z) generate H3(GL3, Z)' (p. 502); 'Suslin proves [183, 4.4.1] that the 2-primary subgroup of H3(Σ6, Z) maps to zero in B(F). We omit the details' (p. 502); and 'Suslin proved in [183, 4.2] that the images of the latter two summands in H3(Mn) are contained in the image of H3(Tn, Z) for large n' (p. 504). Needed: the source, and a decomposition of the degree-three case into nodes of V.4.)

gaps.title: Stable-homotopy inputs of Theorem 5.16 and Proposition 5.17
gaps.detail: Needed: the Barratt–Priddy–Quillen equivalence K(F^×-Sets_fin) ≃ ℤ × BM^+ with its graded ring structure (K-book IV.4.10.1, IV.4.6.1, Ex. IV.1.27, Ex. IV.4.12); π^s_1, π^s_2, π^s_3 ≅ ℤ/24 and η³ = 12ν; BM^+ ≃ BP^+ × B(F^×) × BΣ_2 and π_n(BP^+) ≅ π_n(BM^+) for n ≥ 2 (Ex. IV.1.8); Lemma IV.1.19 for BP^+; π_2(BM^+) ≅ π^s_2 ⊕ ∧̃²F^× (Ex. VI.5.11); and Ex. VI.5.9 and VI.5.13. No atlas stage text names the Barratt–Priddy–Quillen theorem or the stable stems. (Merged by the review with a parallel finding: V.4/pi3-bm-plus and V.4/pi3ind-bm-plus (K-book Theorem VI.5.16 and Proposition VI.5.17, PDF pp. 504–506) use the following inputs: the Barratt–Priddy–Quillen theorem (IV.4.10.1); the identification of Z × BM⁺ with the K-theory space of finite free Fˣ-sets, whose homotopy groups form a graded-commutative ring with π₁(BM⁺) ≅ Fˣ × π^s_1 (Example IV.4.10.1, IV.4.6.1, Ex. IV.1.27); the ring map to K_*(F) (Ex. IV.4.12); π₂(BM⁺) = π^s_2 ⊕ ∧̃²Fˣ (Ex. VI.5.11); the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence E²_{p,q} = H_p(Fˣ, π^s_q) ⇒ π_{p+q}(Z × BM⁺) as a module over π^s_*; and π^s_3/(η³) ≅ Z/12. V.4/symmetric-group-image uses H₃(Σ_∞, Z) ≅ Z/12 ⊕ (Z/2)² (Ex. IV.1.13) and Nakaoka's H₃(Σ₆, Z) ≅ H₃(Σ_∞, Z) ([141]). No stage of the atlas states Barratt–Priddy–Quillen, the K-theory of finite sets or these stable stems; StableHomotopyKTheory H.5 and H.6 plan spectra and exact couples in general.)

gaps.title: Homology of monomial and symmetric groups
gaps.detail: Needed: Ex. VI.5.10 (H_3 of M_n = T_n ⋊ Σ_n by Hochschild–Serre, parts (a) to (e)), Ex. VI.5.12, Suslin [183, 4.2] (two Künneth summands land in the image of H_3(T_n) for large n), H_3(Σ_∞, ℤ) ≅ ℤ/12 ⊕ (ℤ/2)² (Ex. IV.1.13), Nakaoka's H_3(Σ_6, ℤ) ≅ H_3(Σ_∞, ℤ), and Suslin [183, 4.4.1] (the 2-primary part of H_3(Σ_6) maps to zero in B(F)).

gaps.title: The étale Chern class step of Lemma 5.19 has no admissible supplier
gaps.detail: Needed: the e-invariant K_3^ind(F) → H^0(F, μ^{⊗2}) (K-book Definition VI.2.1); the étale Chern class c_{2,4} : K_4(F; ℤ/m) → H^0(F, μ_m^{⊗2}) with c_1(β) = ζ and the product formula; Ex. V.11.5; and K^M_3(F) uniquely divisible and a summand for F algebraically closed (III.7.2, V.11.13). MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8 constructs étale Chern classes ('Construct étale Chern classes … Prove compatibility with … products') but has V.4 as an ancestor (M.8 → BorelRegulators:R.7 → Polylogarithms:P.2 → K3BlochGroups:V.4), so it cannot be a prerequisite. M.7 states rigidity and descent, not Chern classes. ArithmeticKTheory N.5 concerns number fields and S-integers, not algebraically closed fields. (Merged by the review with a parallel finding: The injectivity of the enhanced summand for an algebraically closed field (K-book Lemma VI.5.19, PDF p. 507) uses: the e-invariant of Definition VI.2.1, which rests on K_{2i−1}(F̄)_tors ≅ μ(i) (Prop. VI.1.7.1); the unique divisibility of K^M_3 of an algebraically closed field (III.7.2) and the summand statement V.11.13; the étale Chern class c_{2,4}: K_4(F; Z/m) → H^0(F, μ_m^{⊗2}) with c_1(β) = ζ (V.11.10.1) and the product rule; K_4(F; Z/m) ≅ Z/m on β² (VI.1.4, which rests on the rigidity theorem VI.1.3); the Bockstein isomorphism K_4(F; Z/m) ≅ mK_3(F); and Ex. V.11.5. The packet cited these inputs to MotivicEtaleKTheory M.7 and ArithmeticKTheory N.5, and neither supplies them. M.7 plans étale K-theory, 'the relevant rigidity and étale descent theorems' and Quillen–Lichtenbaum, but no Chern classes, and N.5 concerns number fields and S-integers. Étale Chern classes are planned only by M.8 ('Construct étale Chern classes, real Deligne cycle-class maps and the rational regulator'), which lies downstream of V.4: M.8 requires BorelRegulators R.7, which requires Polylogarithms P.2, which requires K3BlochGroups V.4. They therefore cannot be imported without a cycle (see the restructure proposal). No stage states the e-invariant of an arbitrary field or the isomorphism K_{2i−1}(F̄)_tors ≅ μ(i).)

gaps.title: Suslin's sequence for finite fields is not proved by the sources read
gaps.detail: K-book Theorem VI.5.2 asserts the sequence for |F| ≥ 4, and Remark VI.5.1.1 deduces the orders of B(F_q) for q > 3 from it. The printed proof uses F infinite at Lemma 5.11, Example 5.9.1, Remark 5.12.1 (via IV.1.15) and the T_2 ⊂ B isomorphism, which fails for F_4, and Theorem 5.7 is false for F_4. V.4 is therefore stated for infinite fields, as its stage asks. V.5/bloch-group-finite-field and V.3/small-field-conventions cite V.4/suslin-exact-sequence for finite fields and need another route. (Merged by the review with a parallel finding: K-book Theorem VI.5.2 is stated 'For any field F with |F| ≥4', but its proof collates Theorem 5.16 and Corollary 5.20. Theorem 5.16 rests on Proposition 5.12 and Remark 5.12.1, and these use infinite-field statements: Example 5.9.1 ('if X is infinite then C∗ → Z and hence C∗ → C∗(X) are quasi-isomorphisms'), Lemma 5.11 ('If F is infinite, Hn(T3, Z) → Hn(D∗T3) is zero for n > 0') and IV.1.15 ('If F is an infinite field'). The section gives no argument for finite F. The stage text asks only for infinite fields ('For infinite fields prove the Bloch–Wigner/Suslin exact sequence'). Even so, V.4/suslin-exact-sequence asserts |F| ≥ 4, and V.5/bloch-group-finite-field derives B(F_q) for q > 3 from it, as the K-book's Remark 5.1.1 does. Needed: either the node is restricted to infinite fields and the finite case is sourced separately, or a proof for finite fields is found.) (Review, after the Lean sync: the V.5 and V.6 comparisons stated for fields with at least four elements also rest on this case wherever the field is finite; for infinite fields they follow from V.4.)

gaps.title: The lower bound for the order of c over Q and R uses an unread argument
gaps.detail: That c = [2] + [−1] has order exactly six in B(Q) and B(R) needs a homomorphism out of B(R) that detects it; the K-book cites Suslin [Su91, pp. 219–220] and the Rogers L-function 'built from the dilogarithm function'. The original was not read and no stage plans the Rogers dilogarithm (a request to Polylogarithms P.1 is recorded). The Bloch-Wigner function cannot replace it: it vanishes on P¹(R) and kills torsion. (Merged by the review with a parallel finding: What is missing is not a numerical evaluation. The K-book states: 'In fact, the element c = [2] + [−1] has order exactly 6 in both B(Q) and B(R). This may be proven using the Rogers L-function, which is built from the dilogarithm function. See [187, pp. 219–220]' (VI.5.2.1, PDF p. 496). The Rogers dilogarithm is built from the real dilogarithm, not from the Bloch–Wigner function, which vanishes on real points and so detects nothing in B(R). No stage plans the Rogers dilogarithm or the homomorphism it induces on B(R): Polylogarithms P.1 plans Li_n, the single-valued L_n and D. Suslin [187] was not read. The certified numerics of Polylogarithms P.2 (P.2/certified-numerics) cannot by themselves prove an exact order. Needed: the Rogers dilogarithm with its five-term and reflection relations, the induced homomorphism from B(R) to a circle group and its value on c, taken from [187] or another source. The gap's title should be changed to 'The Rogers-dilogarithm lower bound for the order of c is not planned'; the title is kept here only so that the patch replaces this entry.)

gaps.title: No explicit chain-level lift from a certificate to a bar cycle
gaps.detail: The K-book proves that ψ: H_3(GL_3(F)) → B(F) is onto (Proposition VI.5.12) through the hyperhomology spectral sequence, and that K_3(F) → H_3(SL(F)) is onto (IV.1.20), but gives no chain-level construction of a preimage of a given Bloch element, nor of a lift from H_3(GL(F)) to H_3(St(F)). The existence statement is closed; an explicit transport from a five-term or boundary certificate to a bar 3-cycle is not, and no comparison in this packet requires it.

gaps.title: The finite-field inputs of CGZ §4.2 beyond Suslin's sequence are unowned
gaps.detail: RT-AREA-ktheory-2/13 (confirmed) asks V.5 to supply the finite-field inputs of CGZ's reduction. B(F_q) and B(F_q) ⊗ Z/n ≅ K_3(F_q) ⊗ Z/n for q ≡ −1 mod n are now V.5/bloch-group-finite-field and V.5/bloch-finite-field-mod-n. Still missing: the prime-to-q part of H_3(SL_2(F_q), Z) is cyclic of order q² − 1 (Quillen; CGZ state the whole group, which is false for q = 5, see the source issue), the map H_3(SL_2(F_q), Z) → B(F_q) of Hutchinson (J. K-Theory 12 (2013)) with its isomorphism modulo n, and the explicit non-split-torus element of CGZ equation (33). Neither source was read; the unstable homology of SL_2(F_q) has no owner in the atlas.

gaps.title: The comparison with coefficients, as opposed to modulo n, is not planned
gaps.detail: V.6/comparison-finite-coefficients compares K_3^ind(F)/n with B(F)/n. The comparison of K_3(F; Z/n), which sits in 0 → K_3(F)/n → K_3(F; Z/n) → K_2(F)[n] → 0 and is constructed in HabiroNumberFields HB.1, with CGZ's étale Bloch group B(F; Z/nZ) of equation (14), which sits in 0 → B(F)/nB(F) → B(F; Z/nZ) → K_2(F)[n] → 0 (CGZ Theorem 1.7), is not planned anywhere, and B(F; Z/nZ) has no owner.

gaps.title: The decomposable part of K_3 of a p-adic field modulo p^m
gaps.detail: Transporting D.2's p-adic comparison from K_3^ind(L)/p^m to K_3(L)/p^m needs K_3^M(L)/p^m = 0 for a finite extension L of Q_p, or that the regulator kills decomposables. No stage read states either; the literature result on Milnor K-theory of local fields was not read.

requests.need: The finite-field calculation in the case j = 2, namely that K_3 of a finite field with q elements is cyclic of order q squared minus one, for every q including 2 and 3, together with the restriction and transfer maps in degree three and their formulas in the functorial model, stated without choosing a cyclic generator. L.1 states all of this ('Prove, for every finite field with q elements and every j≥1, … K_{2j−1}(F_q) ≅ Z/(q^j−1)'; 'Construct the restriction and transfer maps for finite extensions and prove their formulas in the functorial model'); V.5 specialises it and must not reprove it.

The certified examples this layer consumes: K_3 of the integers is cyclic of order forty-eight (part of 'Compute the first four groups of Z') and K_3 of the Gaussian rationals is the direct sum of a free group of rank one and a cyclic group of order twenty-four ('compute K₂(Z[i])=0 and K₃(Q(i)) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/24'), with the free summand stated as the existence of a basis. N.8 states both; the ownership overlap with V.5's own 'Prove K₃(Z) ≅ Z/48' is recorded in restructure.

The degree-three row of the odd-group structure theorem, for a number field and for its rings of S-integers, in the two cases totally imaginary and with a real embedding, with the extension data rather than only the abstract group; and the isomorphism K_3(O_{F,S}) ≅ K_3(F) (the case j = 2 of 'Prove K_{2j−1}(O_{F,S}) ≅ K_{2j−1}(F) for j≥2'), which V.2 uses to pass Borel's rank to the field and V.5 uses for K_3(Z) ≅ K_3(Q). N.5 concerns number fields and S-integers only and supplies nothing to the e-invariant step of V.4/pi3ind-bm-plus, which is dropped from neededBy.

The Bloch-Wigner function with its conjugation relation, and its five-term identity in the K-book normalisation, as the nodes Polylogarithms:P.1/bloch-wigner-dilogarithm and Polylogarithms:P.1/bloch-wigner-five-term. The two V.3 nodes with the reserved analytic ids are pointer comparisons importing these; the descent is Polylogarithms:P.2/bloch-wigner-descent. Those Polylogarithms nodes should cite the V.3 node ids (pre-bloch-group, bloch-group) rather than the stage K3BlochGroups:V.3, which removes the stage-level cycle V.3 → P.1 → V.3. The Rogers dilogarithm L(x) = Li_2(x) + ½ log(x) log(1 − x) on (0, 1), its extension to the real line, its reflection and five-term identities, and the resulting homomorphism from B(R), in Suslin's convention of V.3, to R modulo a lattice of rational multiples of π² under which c has image of order six (Suslin, K_3 of a field and the Bloch group, pp. 219–220). P.1's stage text plans Li_n and the Bloch-Wigner function but not this function.

The comparison of the descended Bloch-Wigner map with the Borel class, with its sign and scalar. The Polylogarithms packet plans exactly this as Polylogarithms:P.2/borel-comparison, through P.2/bloch-wigner-descent and P.2/weight-two-regulator, so by PROTOCOL §3 V.6/regulator-agreement should cite that node id rather than the stage. The certified numerics (P.2/certified-numerics) are not needed: the order of c needs the Rogers dilogarithm, not a numerical value (see the gap on the order of c).

The comparison, in degree three and weight two, of the syntomic or étale regulator with the explicit p-adic dilogarithm on the Bloch-group model, with its scalar and Frobenius normalisation and its coefficient hypotheses (D.2's stage text). D.3, the unramified p > 3 theorem, is a consumer of V.6's root-of-unity classes, not a supplier: citing it here would close a cycle once D.3 imports V.6. The comparison, in degree three and weight two, of the étale/syntomic regulator with the explicit p-adic dilogarithm on the Bloch-group model of V.3 and V.6, with its scalar and Frobenius normalisation and the coefficient hypotheses under which it holds. This is D.2's text ('In degree three and weight two compare the regulator with the explicit p-adic dilogarithm on V's Bloch-group model. Give the actual scalar/Frobenius normalisation.'). D.3, named before, proves the unramified p > 3 image theorem D_p: K_3(L; Z_p) ≅ p²O_L, requires K3BlochGroups V.4, and does not state the comparison.

The stable Steinberg group St(A) as the colimit of the St_n(A) with its stabilisation maps, functorial in ring maps; the surjection onto E(A); the general definition of a universal central extension; and the theorem that St(A) → E(A) is a universal central extension with kernel K_2(A), for every associative unital ring with no stable-range hypothesis (K-book III.5.2.1 and III.5.5 have none). V.1 imports these and proves only superperfection and the homotopy-theoretic consequences.

The plus construction with its universal property, homology isomorphism, functoriality and relative form; in particular (i) K-book Ex. IV.1.8: for a perfect normal subgroup P of G, BP⁺ is homotopy equivalent to the universal cover of BG⁺ (plus relative to P), so π_n(BP⁺) ≅ π_n(BG⁺) for n ≥ 2; (ii) the comparison of fibres after plus for a central extension 1 → A → S → P → 1 of perfect groups: BA → BS⁺ → BP⁺ is a homotopy fibration (Ex. IV.1.9); (iii) BM⁺ for the monomial group M and its commutator subgroup, used by V.4. H.3 states the plus construction, its universal property and 'the relative construction needed to compare fibres after applying plus'. It does not state homological stability, which is no longer requested here: V.4's stage text assigns it to V.4 ('prove them here when they are not supplied by H'); see the gap.

Milnor K-theory as the tensor algebra of the units modulo the homogeneous Steinberg ideal, in all degrees, together with the graded map to Quillen K-theory whose degree-three component V.2 uses. The field presentation of K_2 that V.3 needs is requested separately from T.2:symbols.

Suslin's rigidity for algebraically closed fields (K-book Theorem VI.1.3: for algebraically closed k ⊂ F the maps K_n(k; Z/m) → K_n(F; Z/m) are isomorphisms) and its consequence that a Bott element β gives a graded ring isomorphism K_*(F; Z/m) ≅ Z/m[β] for F algebraically closed with 1/m ∈ F (VI.1.4 in characteristic 0, VI.1.3.1(iii) in characteristic p), which V.4/pi3ind-bm-plus uses for K_4(F; Z/m) ≅ Z/m on β² (Lemma VI.5.19). M.7: 'Prove the relevant rigidity and étale descent theorems.' The étale Chern classes the same lemma uses are not in M.7 (only M.8 plans them, and M.8 is downstream of V.4); see the gap on the e-invariant step.

The rank of K_3(O_F) for the ring of integers of a number field, rank r_2 (the case n = 3 ≡ 3 mod 4 of N.3:ranks, which applies BorelRegulators R.3; the reserved node BorelRegulators:R.3/borel-rank-theorem states it). R.3 itself is stated for orders and S-integers, not for the field, so V.2 passes to F through ArithmeticKTheory N.5.
K_2(A) ≅ π_2(BGL(A)⁺) ≅ π_2(BE(A)⁺), naturally in A, for every associative unital ring.
The natural graded ring map K_*^M(F) → K_*(F) from products, with {a,b,c} ↦ [a]·[b]·[c] and its compatibility with Matsumoto's isomorphism under K_1 ⊗ K_2 → K_3; V.2 uses its degree-three component.

Milnor K-theory of a field as the tensor algebra of the units modulo the homogeneous Steinberg ideal, and Matsumoto's theorem that K_2(F) is generated by the symbols {a, b}. For every field F: Matsumoto's presentation K_2(F) ≅ Fˣ ⊗ Fˣ modulo the Steinberg subgroup generated by the x ⊗ (1 − x); anti-commutativity {a, b} = −{b, a}; and {a, a} = {a, −1}. With these, Fˣ ⊗ Fˣ modulo Steinberg equals the antisymmetric quotient modulo the x ∧ (1 − x). The stage text plans exactly these: 'Prove Matsumoto's theorem that the resulting map K₂ᴹ(F) → K₂(F) is an isomorphism … Derive {a,b}=-{b,a}, {a,-a}=0, and the correct formula for {a,a}.'

The K-theory space K(A) with its zero component identified naturally with BGL(A)⁺, so K_n(A) = π_n(BGL(A)⁺) for n ≥ 1. V.1 cites this sub-stage rather than K.2, whose K.2:low-degree-comparisons part requires V.4 and would close a cycle.
The external product K_1(Z) ⊗ K_2(R) → K_3(Z ⊗ R) = K_3(R) for every ring R, used for the product with [−1].

For a discrete group G: BG as the realisation of the nerve of its one-object groupoid, a K(G,1), with the comparison of singular homology of BG with Mathlib's groupHomology (Rep.trivial Z G Z), natural in G.
Homotopy fibres and the long exact sequence of homotopy groups, and the fibration BA → BS → BP of classifying spaces of a group extension.
The stable elementary group E(A) inside GL(A), perfect and normal.
SK_1(F) = 0 for a field, so E(F) = SL(F).

For a field k: the ring isomorphism K_*^M(k) ≅ ⊕ H^i(k, Z(i)) (Nesterenko–Suslin–Totaro), the vanishing H^n(k, Z(1)) = 0 for n ≤ 0 and H^n(k, Z(i)) = 0 for n > i, and functoriality in field extensions.

The motivic spectral sequence for Spec of a field, its multiplicative structure, the identification of the edge maps with the Milnor-to-Quillen maps (K-book VI.4.3), and the low-degree exact sequence K_4(k) → H^0(k, Z(2)) → K_3^M(k) → K_3(k) → H^1(k, Z(2)) → 0 (VI.4.3.1).
The identification H^0(k, Z/2(2)) ≅ H^0_et(k, μ_2^{⊗2}) for char k ≠ 2 (the case n = 0 ≤ i = 2 of the motivic-to-étale comparison), used in the proof of Proposition VI.4.3.2.
Finite generation of K_3(O_F) for the ring of integers of a number field.

The absolute Hurewicz theorem in degrees two and three and its naturality, for the classifying spaces and plus constructions of StableHomotopyKTheory (realised as topological spaces); cited in a gap because tauceti:-prefixed ids cannot be prerequisites.
K_2(F_q) = 0 for every finite field F_q (T.5's stage text: 'Prove K₂(Z) ≅ Z/2 with generator {−1,−1}, K₂(F_q)=0'), from which V.5 deduces K_3^M(F_q) = 0.

The spectral sequence of a filtered spectrum, in the form of the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence E^2_{p,q} = H_p(G, π^s_q) ⇒ π_{p+q}(Σ^∞ BG_+) for a discrete group G, as a module spectral sequence over π^s_*, with its convergence for connective spectra.

restructure.title: The two analytic nodes of V.3 are owned by Polylogarithms P.1 and P.2
restructure.detail: The ownership is fixed by the stage texts. P.1: 'For weight two define the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm … Prove conjugation, inversion, the five-term identity and the differential formula.' P.2: 'Descend the Bloch–Wigner function through the exact V.3 Bloch-group convention.' V.3 plans nothing analytic; its only mention is 'Do not erase 2- or 3-torsion merely because the real dilogarithm kills it.' The Polylogarithms packet already contains P.1/bloch-wigner-dilogarithm, P.1/bloch-wigner-five-term and P.2/bloch-wigner-descent, with a matching restructure entry. So the descent belongs to P.2, not P.1. Proposal: retire the reserved ids K3BlochGroups:V.3/bloch-wigner-dilogarithm and K3BlochGroups:V.3/bloch-wigner-five-term from reserved-ids.json; until then they are pointer comparisons carrying only V.3's torsion warning. Consumers to re-point: V.6/regulator-agreement to Polylogarithms:P.2/borel-comparison, the node that states the agreement with the Borel class with its sign and scalar (through P.2/bloch-wigner-descent); V.5/k3-Q-splitting to the Rogers-dilogarithm argument of Suslin [187, pp. 219–220], because D vanishes on real points and cannot detect the order of c. No stage plans the Rogers dilogarithm; see the gap on the order of c. The Polylogarithms nodes cite the stage K3BlochGroups:V.3 and should cite V.3 node ids instead, to break the stage-level cycle.

restructure.title: The comparison of the CGZ and Suslin Bloch-group conventions is owned by K3BlochGroups V.3
restructure.detail: Two stage texts plan the same comparison. K3BlochGroups V.3: 'Separately construct the conventions used by Bloch, Goncharov and Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier. Prove the comparison maps, their exact small torsion corrections and their rational identifications.' HabiroNumberFields HB.1: 'Compare CGZ's Bloch group with V's Suslin convention. Define the actual maps and identify the bounded 2-/6-primary differences.' The reviewed library audit (data/library-coverage.json, layer K3BlochGroups:V.3, duplicates) flags the overlap. Proposal: V.3 owns the definitions and the comparison (cgz-bloch-group, exterior-kernel-bloch-group, exterior-kernel-discrepancy, cgz-degenerate-relations, cgz-convention-comparison); HB.1 is narrowed to import them and keeps the finite-coefficient Chern classes and the CGZ arithmetic statements.

restructure.title: V.6's regulator sentence is owned by Polylogarithms P.2 and PadicHodgeRegulators D.2
restructure.detail: V.6's stage text ends 'Prove that P's real regulator and D's p-adic regulator agree with the abstract K-theory regulators under these comparisons.' Polylogarithms P.2 plans the real comparison ('compare it with the Borel class ... The comparison includes its sign and scalar') and has the node P.2/borel-comparison; PadicHodgeRegulators D.2 plans the p-adic one ('In degree three and weight two compare the regulator with the explicit p-adic dilogarithm on V's Bloch-group model'). The reviewed audit AUDIT-29 lists both as duplicates of V.6, and RT-AREA-ktheory-2/23 and RT-AUDIT-26/4 are confirmed. Proposal: V.6 keeps the rational, integral and modulo-n comparisons and the transport of P.2's and D.2's statements along them (V.6/regulator-agreement, V.6/regulator-agreement-padic); the analytic comparisons stay with P.2 and D.2. Add the atlas links P.2 → V.6 and D.2 → V.6 (both acyclic) and V.6 → D.3, since D.3's text consumes 'V's valid coefficient-localised or integral multiples' (V.6/root-of-unity-class); V.6 → HabiroNumberFields:HB.1 likewise for the modulo-n comparison.

restructure.title: K₃ of finite fields, of the integers and of the Gaussian rationals are owned by KTheoryFiniteLocalFields L.1 and ArithmeticKTheory N.8
restructure.detail: V.5 reads 'Use Quillen's finite-field calculation to construct K₃(F_q) ≅ Z/(q²−1), including q=2 and q=3 … Compute restriction and transfer through the finite-field model. Prove K₃(Z) ≅ Z/48 and K₃(Q) ≅ Z/48 … Include K₃(Q(i)) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/24 as an arithmetic test once N and R are available.' The same results are planned elsewhere. L.1: 'Prove, for every finite field with q elements and every j≥1, … K_{2j−1}(F_q) ≅ Z/(q^j−1)' and 'Construct the restriction and transfer maps for finite extensions and prove their formulas in the functorial model.' N.8: 'Compute the first four groups of Z; compute K₂(Z[i])=0 and K₃(Q(i)) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/24.' N.5: 'Prove K_{2j−1}(O_{F,S}) ≅ K_{2j−1}(F) for j≥2.' The reviewed library audit (data/library-coverage.json, layer K3BlochGroups:V.5, duplicates L.1 and N.8; and conversely under L.1 and N.8) flags both overlaps. The packet already imports these results (V.5/k3-finite-field, V.5/finite-field-transfer, V.5/k3-Z-and-Q, V.5/k3-gaussian). Proposal: L.1 and N.8 own them, and V.5 is narrowed to the degree-three specialisations and the Bloch-group and decomposable-class bookkeeping (V.5/bloch-group-finite-field, V.5/k3-Q-splitting, V.5/k3-number-field), keeping K₃(Q(i)) as a consistency check against V.5/k3-number-field.

restructure.title: The regulator agreements of V.6 are proved by Polylogarithms P.2 and PadicHodgeRegulators D.2
restructure.detail: V.6 reads 'Prove that P's real regulator and D's p-adic regulator agree with the abstract K-theory regulators under these comparisons.' Two other stages plan the same proofs. P.2: 'Assemble its embedding-wise map for a number field and compare it with the Borel class … The comparison includes its sign and scalar.' D.2: 'In degree three and weight two compare the regulator with the explicit p-adic dilogarithm on V's Bloch-group model. Give the actual scalar/Frobenius normalisation.' The reviewed library audit (layer K3BlochGroups:V.6, duplicates Polylogarithms:P.2 and PadicHodgeRegulators:D.2; and under Polylogarithms:P.2) flags both, and the Polylogarithms packet already plans Polylogarithms:P.2/borel-comparison. V.6/regulator-agreement exports the statement only and says the proofs 'belong to Polylogarithms P.2 and PadicHodgeRegulators D.2'. Proposal: P.2 and D.2 own the two agreements. V.6 is narrowed to the rational, integral and finite-coefficient comparisons and the statement of which comparison each regulator uses. V.6/regulator-agreement cites Polylogarithms:P.2/borel-comparison and PadicHodgeRegulators:D.2, not D.3. D.3's text consumes V.6 ('The roots-of-unity classes are constructed through V's valid coefficient-localised or integral multiples'), but D.3 requires only V.4. Once V.6 no longer cites D.3, a link V.6 → D.3 can be recorded without a cycle.

restructure.title: The configuration complex and the cross-ratio are owned by K3BlochGroups V.4
restructure.detail: V.4 reads 'Develop the configuration complex for points in the projective line, its group action and spectral sequence, the cross-ratio map, and the identification of the homology terms.' P.2 reads 'Develop the configuration/cross-ratio cocycle and hyperbolic-volume calculation used by Bloch to identify this map with the abstract regulator.' The reviewed library audit flags the overlap under both layers. The Polylogarithms packet already imports the machinery ('the configuration and cross-ratio machinery is imported from K3BlochGroups V.4, which owns it', Polylogarithms:P.2/hyperbolic-volume) and requests from V.4 'The configuration complex of points of the projective line, the cross-ratio and Suslin's exact sequence'. Proposal: V.4 owns the configuration complex and the cross-ratio map, which therefore needs a construction node of its own in V.4. P.2 is narrowed to the Bloch–Wigner cocycle and the volume identification.

restructure.title: The explicit K₃ model is owned by K3BlochGroups V.1 and V.4; GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2:low-degree-comparisons imports it
restructure.detail: K.2:low-degree-comparisons reads 'Combine them with U, T and V to identify the explicit K₁, K₂ and K₃ models', and it requires K3BlochGroups:V.4. The reviewed library audit (layer K3BlochGroups:V.1, duplicates) records it as making 'the comparison K₃(A) ≅ H₃(St(A), ℤ) made here'. The packet had expressed this as a request to GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.2, which cannot supply V.4: K.2 contains K.2:low-degree-comparisons, so V.4 → K.2 → K.2:low-degree-comparisons → V.4 is a stage cycle. Proposal: V.1/k3-h3-steinberg and V.4/suslin-exact-sequence own the explicit K₃ model, and K.2:low-degree-comparisons imports them. The K3BlochGroups layers cite only K.2:plus from that stage.

restructure.title: Étale Chern classes on K-theory with finite coefficients are needed upstream of V.4
restructure.detail: Suslin's sequence needs the enhanced summand to inject into K₃^ind(F). The K-book proves this in Lemma VI.5.19 with the étale Chern class c_{2,4}: K_4(F; Z/m) → H^0(F, μ_m^{⊗2}), its product rule and c_1(β) = ζ. The only stage that plans étale Chern classes is MotivicEtaleKTheory M.8 ('Construct étale Chern classes, real Deligne cycle-class maps and the rational regulator from motivic cohomology'). M.8 requires BorelRegulators R.7, which requires Polylogarithms P.2, which requires K3BlochGroups V.4, so V.4 cannot import them. Proposal: split M.8 so that the étale Chern classes c_{i,j} on K_j(X; Z/m), with the product formula and the value on the Bott element, form a sub-stage that does not depend on R.7, for example beside M.7, which V.4/pi3ind-bm-plus then cites.

sourceIssues.locator: The K-book, author-hosted draft of 29 August 2013, Theorem VI.5.7 (PDF p. 498)
sourceIssues.printed: Note: there was a typo in the published version.)
sourceIssues.correction: The parenthetical note is the author's own, flagging a typographical error in the published Graduate Studies in Mathematics printing of the same theorem. A reader working from the published book should take the statement in the form given in this draft: the first homology of the group of invertible two by two matrices is the units of the field, the second homology is the direct sum of the exterior square of the units and K_2 of the field, and the displayed sequence from the third homology of the monomial subgroup through the third homology of the general linear group onto the Bloch group is exact. (Review: the corrected form itself holds only for infinite F; for F₄, H₂(GL₂(F₄), ℤ) ≅ ℤ/2 while ∧²F₄× ⊕ K₂(F₄) = 0, recorded separately.)

sourceIssues.printed: Theorem 5.7. For all F, H1(GL2(F), Z) = F×, H2(GL2(F), Z) = (∧2 F×) ⊕ K2(F) and there is a map ψ and an exact sequence
sourceIssues.correction: For all infinite F. The H_2 formula fails for F = F_4 (and H_1 fails for F_2, which Remark 5.1.1 excludes).
sourceIssues.reason: GL_2(F_4) ≅ F_4^× × SL_2(F_4) ≅ ℤ/3 × A_5, so H_2(GL_2(F_4), ℤ) ≅ H_2(A_5, ℤ) ≅ ℤ/2 by Künneth, while ∧²(F_4^×) ⊕ K_2(F_4) = ∧²(ℤ/3) ⊕ 0 = 0. sourceIssues.correction: C∗(X) is the subcomplex of injective tuples in the chain complex of eC(X); it is closed under faces and rotations but not under degeneracies (a precyclic abelian group), and it is not the Dold–Kan complex of eC(X). The acyclicity of the complex that omits the last face must be proved by the prepending homotopy for infinite X, not by the extra degeneracy of a cyclic set.
sourceIssues.reason: For X = {x, y}, the normalised complex of Z[X^{n+1}] is acyclic in positive degrees (the simplicial set with n-simplices X^{n+1} is contractible, and (x, y, x) is a nondegenerate 2-simplex), while C∗(X) = (Z² → Z²) has H1 ≅ Z generated by (x, y) + (y, x).

sourceIssues.locator: The K-book, draft of 29 August 2013, proof of Lemma VI.5.14 (PDF p. 503) and Exercise VI.5.5 (PDF p. 508)
sourceIssues.correction: f2(1) = (∞, 0, x) + (1, ∞, x) + (0, 1, x). The last two terms are [(x − 1)/(xy)] and [y/((1 − x)(y − 1))]. The choice needs x ≠ 2 as well (otherwise y = w). The expression becomes −[x²] − 2[−x^{−1}] + 2[x − 1] + [(1 − x)^{−2}], and Ex. 5.5's second identity should read [x²] + 2[−x^{−1}] − 2[x − 1] − [(1 − x)^{−2}] = 2c.
sourceIssues.reason: Evaluating f3(1) by cross-ratios gives the corrected terms (checked numerically over C). The Bloch–Wigner function kills torsion, and it is nonzero on the printed six-term expression and on the printed final expression, so neither can equal the 3-torsion element −2c. In P(Fp), p = 5, …, 23, the corrected expressions equal −2c (respectively 2c) for every admissible x, and the printed ones fail, e.g. in P(F5) at x = 3. With y = x−1 = w (x = 2) the tuple (1, ∞, w, y) is degenerate. The conclusion of Lemma 5.14 stands.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 4.4 and its proof, pp. 24-25, arXiv:1712.04887v3
sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 4.4. Let p > 2. There is a commutative diagram as follows: [left column B(F)/nB(F) = K3(F)/nK3(F)] ... Proof. The isomorphism of the left vertical map is a theorem of Suslin [30, Theorem 5.2] (taking into account Lemma 2.2)
sourceIssues.correction: The left vertical isomorphism B(F)/nB(F) ≅ K_3(F)/nK_3(F) needs µ(F) ⊗ Z/p = 0, i.e. ζ_p ∉ F; this holds under the hypothesis ζ ∉ F̃(ζ + ζ^{−1}) of Proposition 4.2 and under Theorem 1.2's hypothesis.
sourceIssues.reason: Reducing Suslin's sequence modulo n leaves the image of µ̃(F)/n in the kernel. For F = Q(√−3) and p = n = 3: K_3(F) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/24 (K-book Corollary VI.5.3(a), w_2 = 24), µ̃(F) ≅ Z/12, so B(F) ≅ Z ⊕ Z/2 and B(F)/3 ≅ Z/3, while K_3(F)/3 ≅ (Z/3)².

sourceIssues.printed: By a computation of Quillen, we know that H3(SL2(Fq), Z) is cyclic of order q2 −1.
sourceIssues.correction: The part of H_3(SL_2(F_q), Z) prime to q is cyclic of order q² − 1; the whole group has additional q-primary torsion.
sourceIssues.reason: For q = 5, which the section allows (5 ≡ −1 mod 3), SL_2(F_5) is the binary icosahedral group of order 120; it acts freely on S³, so it has periodic cohomology and H_3(SL_2(F_5), Z) ≅ Z/120, not Z/24. Likewise SL_2(F_3), of order 24, has H_3 ≅ Z/24, not Z/8.

sourceIssues.locator: The K-book, author-hosted draft of 29 August 2013, paragraph 5.8.2 in the proof of Theorem VI.5.7, PDF p. 499
sourceIssues.printed: By the Künneth formula [223, 6.1.13], Hn(T2) ≅ ⊕i+j=n Hi(F×) ⊗ Hj(F×), with σ interchanging the factors
sourceIssues.correction: Integrally H_n(T₂) ≅ ⊕_{i+j=n} H_i(Fˣ) ⊗ H_j(Fˣ) ⊕ ⊕_{i+j=n−1} Tor₁^ℤ(H_i(Fˣ), H_j(Fˣ)). The Tor summand vanishes for n ≤ 2, the degree the proof computes (H₂(T₂)_σ ≅ ∧²Fˣ ⊕ ∧̃²Fˣ); for n = 3 it contains Tor₁^ℤ(Fˣ, Fˣ) ≅ Tor₁^ℤ(μ(F), μ(F)), which is nonzero whenever F has a nontrivial root of unity.
sourceIssues.reason: For F = F_5, Fˣ ≅ ℤ/4 has H₀, …, H₃ = ℤ, ℤ/4, 0, ℤ/4. The displayed formula gives H₃(T₂) ≅ (ℤ/4)², while the Künneth theorem for the free bar complexes gives (ℤ/4)² ⊕ Tor₁(ℤ/4, ℤ/4) ≅ (ℤ/4)³. The proof uses only H₂(T₂), and of H₃(T₂) only that the relevant term is 'a quotient Q3 of H3(T2)σ', which the missing summand does not change.

review.notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-38267a, of the packet by session cc-7b31c4. Six checkers read the sources (Weibel, The K-book, author draft of 29 Aug 2013, SHA-256 a04f53c9…; Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier arXiv:1712.04887v3, SHA-256 024317c2…, and its TeX) against every node: V.1–V.2, V.3, V.4, V.5–V.6, the packet-level items (baseline, library audit, requests, gaps, coverage, restructure, reserved ids, test kinds) and the suggested Lean file. The coordinator re-derived the finite-field Bloch-group computations by an independent Smith normal form computation, checked the stage graph for cycles, fetched Weibel's errata file (Wayback copy), and compiled the suggested file. Corrected: 60 of the 62 nodes (2 verified unchanged); added: 40 nodes. Main corrections: V.4 is stated for infinite fields (Theorem 5.7's H_2 formula fails for F_4) and Suslin's sequence for finite fields is a gap; ⟨x⟩ lies in P(F), not B(F); the CGZ comparison κ is neither injective nor surjective in general (kernel and cokernel 2-groups); V.2's injectivity of Milnor K_3 is the K-book's motivic argument with its inputs made explicit, not an import from M.7; stage-level prerequisites that closed cycles (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory K.2, Polylogarithms P.2 in V.3) were removed; the Bloch–Wigner nodes are pointer comparisons owned by Polylogarithms P.1/P.2; every unit test has its §12 kind; baseline 33 → 89 declarations, every one checked at the pinned commits, and Matrix.card_GL_field removed as unused. The suggested Lean file was rewritten to elaborate against Mathlib 082e2d3 with unproved-declaration warnings only; its 29 True placeholders were replaced by honest statements. Source issues: E1 confirmed and marked as a known erratum; E2–E30 new, all checked at their locators. Open: 23 gaps and 27 requests, recorded with neededBy; a cross-packet cycle (Polylogarithms P.1/bloch-wigner-five-term rests on the stage K3BlochGroups:V.3) is left to that packet's owner by a restructure entry.
